# The avian syrinx

- Located at junction of bronchi and trachea (c.f. **larynx** at top of neck)
- Sounds produced by forcing air through syrinx, reducing static pressure on syringeal membranes flanking interclavicular air sac (Bernoulli effect!)

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.9\linewidth]{images/syrinx.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny [*Cornell*](https://www.macaulaylibrary.org/2021/09/27/body-size-and-bill-size-and-shape-affect-tanager-song-characteristics/)

# Syrinx anatomy varies with vocal ability

- L: typical oscine songbird syrinx with both **tracheal** and **bronchial** elements
- R: suboscine song syrinx with only tracheal elements

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.9\linewidth]{images/syrinx_comp.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Goller 2022)

# Syrinx evolution

- ancestor of birds lost ability to makes sounds with **larynx**, re-evolved ability with **syrinx** (an **evolutionary novelty**)

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.9\linewidth]{images/syrinx_evol.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Kinglsey et al. 2018)

# Bird song physics

- **amplitude**: height of soundwaves = "loudness"
- **frequency**: distance between peaks of soundwaves = pitch

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.9\linewidth]{images/spectrograms.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny [*Cornell*](https://academy.allaboutbirds.org/birdsong/)

# Harmonics

- Multiple sound producing areas in syrinx = multiple simultaneous notes
- Harmonics are multiples of a "fundamental frequency"

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.7\linewidth]{images/canyon.jpg}
\end{figure}  

https://macaulaylibrary.org/asset/224190551

\hfill \tiny (Bilger et al. 2021)

# Post-source modulation

- **filtering** eliminates or enhances certain vocal frequencies by interference with features in vocal cavity (e.g., bill)
-  **post-source modulation** refers to altering sounds from syrinx via changes in length, shape, size of vocal cavity

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.7\linewidth]{images/crane_trachea.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Cous 1882)  

# Feeding ecology constrains song

- Bill size reflects adaptations to seed size 
- High rate, pure-tone trills are physically impossible for birds with large bills

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.8\linewidth]{images/billsize.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Podos 2001)

# Chickadees encode information on predator size in song

- Number of harmonic "dees" negatively correlates to predator body size (smaller = bigger threat)

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = \linewidth]{images/chickadee.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Podos 2001)

# Binaural comparison to locate predators

- **aerial predators** (top): limited amplitude, long waves scatter, difficult to source
- **ground predators** (bottom): large amplitude, short, lots of location information

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.7\linewidth]{images/chicken_call.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny ([*Gallus gallus* calls, Aves Biology / Gary Ritchison](https://avesbiology.com/vocalcommunication.html))

# Acoustic adaptation hypothesis

- $H_1$: Birds in denser habitats will have lower calls
- Methods: Meta-analysis of frequencies paired with habitat cover 

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = \linewidth]{images/acoustic_1.png}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}

c) impossible to say
d) it depends

(But see: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iy-9Z2KrjsY)

\hfill \tiny (Mikula et al. 2021)

# Vocal learning is rare but has evolved multiple times

- Found in parrots, songbirds, hummingbirds, humans, bats, and whales

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.45\linewidth]{images/vocal_learning.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Petkov & Jarvis 2012) 


# Phases of song learning

- **sensory acquisition phase**: innate "template" modified by auditory environment 
- **sensorimotor phase**: practices **subsong** to develop **plastic** (flexible but compelete) song
- **crystalized phase**: stable adult song

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.8\linewidth]{images/learning.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Brainard & Doupe 2002) 

# Phases of song learning

- White-crowned Sparrows only use phrases from "tutors"

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = \linewidth]{images/wcsp.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Rose et al. 2004)

# Learned song variation

- **dialects**: geographically constrained song variants 
- **repertoire**: the set of songs an individual knows

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.5\linewidth]{images/dialects.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Nelson et al. 2004)
